title: No reclass when the bill already sits on the work order's account
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Make sure Require Review Before Completion is off in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Complete, with one special-order part whose vendor bill of $125.00 posted to account X.
custom_steps:
1. Open work order 1.
  2. Click Close Work Order in the work order header.
  3. Click Close Work Order in the confirmation.
  4. In QuickBooks Online, open the journal entries for work order 1's number.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Work order 1 opens.

Step 2:

  • The Close confirmation opens.

Step 3:

  • The work order shows the status Closed.

Step 4:

  • No reclass entry is sent for the bill.
  • The bill line stays on account X.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R4: “When a vendor bill was posted to Cost of Parts (or a category account) and the work order later becomes internal or no charge, Close adds a reclass journal entry: debit the mapped expense account, credit the account the bill line was posted to, for that bill's lines. When a vendor bill was posted to one expense account and the work order closes under the other classification, Close adds a reclass from the account the bill line was posted to, to the work order's mapped account; no reclass when both resolve to the same account. When a vendor bill was posted to an expense account and the work order becomes billable, invoicing adds the reverse entry: debit the account the bill would post to today, credit that expense account.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
